usage: 외 marks the mother's side of the family
댁 is the polite word for house
닮다 = resemble; 닮았어요 = I take after him
examples: My uncle (mom's brother) is a doctor.
I meet my maternal uncle on holidays.
My maternal uncle helps me a lot.
nuance: 외삼촌 is your mother's brother; the 외 prefix means 'maternal side' and shows up in many kinship words. The father's brother is just 삼촌, so the prefix is what separates the two sides. Koreans use these precise terms constantly, so beginners should learn the pair together.
mistakes: Dropping 외 and saying 삼촌, which points to the father's side instead
Confusing 외삼촌 (mom's brother) with 외숙모, who is his wife

usage: 들어오다 = come in; set phrase for marrying in
(며느리를) 보다 = to get a daughter-in-law (when a son marries)
examples: 이에요/예요 = is; spoken by the in-laws
My son brought home a daughter-in-law.
nuance: 며느리 is the word the husband's parents use for their son's wife. It only makes sense from the in-laws' point of view, so a wife does not call herself 며느리 to her own friends in casual chat. The phrase 며느리를 보다 ('to see a daughter-in-law') is the idiomatic way to say a son has married.
mistakes: Confusing 며느리 (son's wife) with 사위 (daughter's husband)
Using 며느리 from the wife's own viewpoint; it is how the in-laws refer to her

usage: (사위를) 보다 = to get a son-in-law (when a daughter marries)
오다 = come; common at family visits
examples: My son-in-law is an office worker.
회사원 = office worker; spoken by the in-laws
My son-in-law visits the house often.
My daughter brought home a good son-in-law.
nuance: 사위 is the word the wife's parents use for their daughter's husband, the male counterpart to 며느리. Like 며느리, it is defined from the in-laws' side, so a husband does not introduce himself as 사위 in everyday conversation. Saying 사위를 보다 is the set phrase for a daughter getting married.
mistakes: Confusing 사위 (daughter's husband) with 며느리 (son's wife)
Using 사위 about yourself; it is how your wife's parents refer to you

usage: 통하다 = go through; how introductions happen
많다 = many; suggests a wide network
가깝다 = close; someone you know fairly well
examples: 지인을 통해 그 일을 알게 됐어요.
I found out about that job through an acquaintance.
알게 되다 = come to know; 통해 = through
I'm meeting an acquaintance this weekend.
That person is an acquaintance from work.
nuance: 지인 means an acquaintance, someone you know but who is not a close friend (친구). It sounds a bit formal and is common in writing, news, and polite speech, often in phrases like 지인을 통해 (through an acquaintance). Calling someone 지인 keeps a respectful, neutral distance compared to the warmth of 친구.
mistakes: Using 지인 for a close friend; that warmer relationship is 친구
Treating 지인 as very casual; it leans formal and is common in writing
